title: What Göbekli Tepe was for
summary: Findings since 2019 suggest people lived at the site, but no definitive purpose has been found for its megalithic enclosures, popularly called the world's first temples.
why: Monumental building by people without clear farming challenges the old order of farming first, monuments later.

notes.problem: Settlement vs sanctuary is now largely answered (source: settlement inhabited 9500-8000 BCE, domestic structures); what stays open is the enclosures' purpose.

question: Was Göbekli Tepe a ritual sanctuary for hunter-gatherers or a lived-in settlement?
evidence: Built and used c. 9500 to at least 8000 BCE; Schmidt called it a sanctuary with few residents; 2019 findings suggest a settlement with domestic structures.
wouldSettle: Wide excavation of surrounding areas showing year-round houses, hearths and household waste, or their absence.

theories.name: Cult sanctuary
theories.idea: Schmidt saw it as a sanctuary used by nomads, with few or no permanent inhabitants.

theories.name: Settlement with ritual buildings
theories.idea: Newer finds suggest people lived there, challenging the strictly cultic view.
